headline: The planning board in Westfield, Massachusetts, has refused to extend the permit for a 3 billion dollar data centre project, ending the plan for now.
score_reason: Lowered from 5 to 4: the board voted on 13 Oct 2026, three days before the window, and it is a single local project.
importance_line: Westfield residents and officials keep a very large data centre out for now, while the developer blamed state tax incentive delays and federal tariffs, which the board rejected, in a state where communities are slowing data centre plans.
summary: Boston.com reports that Westfield's planning board voted unanimously on 13 Oct 2026 not to extend the special permit, due to expire at the end of October, for developer Servistar Realties' 3 billion dollar hyperscale (very large) data centre on more than 150 acres, saying the company had made little progress since 2019 and had never bought the land. Servistar has 20 days to appeal, and the decision effectively ends large-scale data centre development in Westfield for now, because the City Council already approved a one-year moratorium in July.
notes: Read in full. The text names Massachusetts communities, Gov. Maura Healey and the Hampden County Registry of Deeds. Board vote Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, three days before the window.
